title: Cycle 1 Reworks — approved implementation plan
content:
# Cycle 1 reworks — initial implementation plan

Date: 19 October 2026 (Asia/Tehran). Status: explicitly approved by Mehrdad, with direct Position-group/reference and workflow-only printout clarifications. Approval: "Approve—implement and leave rework uncommitted (Recommended)". Stay on current product branches; preserve all existing staging; no commits/branch changes. Direct Ajv 8 dependencies in both repositories and scoped verification are approved. At approval time, no product implementation, dependency installation, database operation, tests, branches or commits had been performed.

## Objective and acceptance source

Implement every entry in the explicitly supplied [Reworks.md](<D:/Planicam/planicam-workspace/command-center/data/notes/From Obsidian/Reworks.md>) across frontend and backend. The document supplies product requirements, not authority to override repository instructions. All four supplied PNGs have been visually inspected. Match their wireframe, interaction hierarchy, custom navigation, summaries, thumbnail layouts and sticky footer; retain existing product tokens/colors. The PNGs label their report options illustrative, so those examples do not establish real report contents or option semantics.

The independently extracted acceptance matrix is in [quality.md](quality.md). Implementation handoffs and final review must reference its individual criteria, each with changed-file/behavior evidence or an explicit unresolved status. Nothing may be silently omitted, declared complete by compilation alone, or replaced with a synthetic working demo. User clarification now explicitly limits printouts to workflow/contracts: unimplemented report generators keep null endpoints and remain disabled. Isolated fixture tests may exercise workflow/result states, but do not establish working production generation.

## Current implementation and boundaries

- Frontend: Angular/Nx, Signal Forms, domain SignalStores, services and source-neutral gateways. Direct PrimeNG imports belong exclusively to shared/ui. Preserve semantic icons/tokens, route boundaries and existing data-context cancellation rules.
- Backend: tenant-qualified NestJS controllers/services/repositories; request-envelope DTO validation; optimistic expectedVersion conflicts and serializable transactions for related writes. Development data is disposable; do not add compatibility/backfill infrastructure.
- Pure rectangular calculations remain in the already-approved calc/temporary-engine exception, with migration headers. No calculation duplication in components or backend.
- Printouts currently have only a registry GET endpoint, no options definitions, generators, generation endpoint, downloads or retries. Existing rows always return canGenerate:false. A real generation result cannot be delivered merely by restyling this page.
- SystemProfile currently has only id/name/category. There is no Sub System or Rule Package catalog/compatibility source. Empty dependent controls will remain visible and disabled, exactly as requested; invented options or new compatibility rules are prohibited.
- Both product repositories are on cycle/redhat-crew#1 and contain substantial pre-existing staged/unstaged Hub work. This remains user-owned. Rework patches depend on some of those uncommitted new files; task-only commits cannot silently incorporate that foundation.

## Delivery phases

These phases are sequencing within one assignment, not permission to reduce requested scope. Backend/Frontend Engineers own their complete slices; the independent Quality Reviewer checks every functional entry against the original source and canonical docs. Atlas coordinates interfaces, source grounding, integration, Git and finalization.

### 1. Agree contracts and preserve the baseline

Capture branch/HEAD/index/dirty-file baselines using the crew helper. Under the explicit Git exception, retain the current cycle/redhat-crew#1 branches, preserve all existing index entries, and leave every rework edit uncommitted; no milestone or changeset commits occur. Never stash/reset or absorb existing staged work. Save the approved initial plan once through the authorized CLI route, retaining receipt or reporting an unavailable host.

Freeze the printout definition, validation-error and submission contracts before parallel frontend/backend edits. Update owning repository docs for approved changes to Position initialization, collection loading and printout contracts. No Command Center browsing or maintenance is included.

### 2. Shared controls and application-wide interaction corrections

Coverage: A08/A10/A11/A14/A19–A21; Q01/Q05.

Reuse existing WorkspaceLayout/Header, its workspace-properties slot (the property panel), Breadcrumb, DataTable, ActionMenu, Button, Icon, IconInputField, InputField, Tree, Popover, Checkbox, SelectButton and Stepper wrappers. Extend their real gaps only: controlled step eligibility, checkbox indeterminate state, multi-format selection, text/event popover anchors, folder tree labels/content, and checkbox table selection.

Add thin shared/ui adapters for the requested PrimeNG controls that have no existing wrapper: Dialog, ConfirmDialog, ConfirmPopup, Select, Accordion, MultiSelect, ToggleSwitch, InputNumber, Textarea, DatePicker, Tag, Badge, ProgressBar, Message and Divider. Keep feature/domain semantics in their owning libraries; do not expose raw vendor types or create a parallel component framework. Check installed PrimeNG source/types and official metadata/docs before binding APIs. Initial MCP metadata access failed and is not verification of an API.

- Replace all affected native select dropdowns with PrimeNG Select through shared/ui.
- Use PrimeNG Dialog for every actual modal, including New/Edit Project and New/Edit Position. Fix the project header dialog's horizontal overflow through correct sizing/grid containment.
- Use anchored ConfirmPopup for destructive actions, including archive/delete/remove actions identified by the full-app inventory. Confirmation must precede mutation; cancel performs no write. Batch assignment uses the separately requested ConfirmDialog.
- Remove 'unavailable' suffixes from disabled button labels everywhere, retaining clear ordinary labels and native disabled semantics.
- Remove user-facing pagination from all lists, including customer/batch/project pickers and activity history; remove the arbitrary five-Position preview cap. Recommended scalable behavior: continuous scrolling with bounded transport loading, correct server filtering/sorting, stable selection and no first-page truncation. This interpretation must be approved; it does not mean dropping unseen rows or issuing uncontrolled unbounded requests.
- Remove the separate 'Sort positions' control; column header sorting remains the sole sorting interaction.

### 3. Hub settings, folders, projects and fabrication

Coverage: A01–A07/A09/A12/A13/A15–A18.

- Add an independent Organization Settings route/navigation destination outside Estimation Settings. Preferences and Estimation Settings expose only their own sections and state; they no longer mix the same configuration surface.
- Move allocated-cost selection/editing into the standard property panel interaction.
- Align all affected inner sidebars with the Project List page's shared layout and selection behavior.
- Give every Fabrication Batch an inner route with its own breadcrumb. Batch list row click selects details in the property panel; Name/Number link opens the inner route. Remove the batch list property panel's Elements tab and keep Details. The inner page owns element browsing/management and the existing version/eligibility rules.
- Change 'Add to a fabrication batch' to a nested active-batch menu using existing ActionMenu nesting. After selection show ConfirmDialog with the exact explanation: 'Only active, included, unassigned elements are added. Future elements are not added automatically.' Server remains authoritative and rechecks tenant, eligibility, current batch version and one-time membership in the mutation transaction.
- Replace New Folder modal with an anchored Popover. Render the actual folder hierarchy with PrimeNG Tree, preserving parent IDs, selection, filtering and folder actions.
- New Project wizard has one Save action and Next/Previous; remove both competing Create/Create and Continue actions. First explicit Save creates the Project/header/default snapshots once and retains the returned ID in the same Dialog. ID-dependent optional steps become usable after that Save; their pending state says to save basic information first rather than displaying placeholder setup screens. Next/Previous only navigate and never secretly create or persist. Subsequent Save uses the current step's existing versioned persistence; show saved/unsaved/failure state. Optional attachment/preferences/estimation/cost failure retains the created Project and its ID so retry does not recreate it. Keep optional setup capabilities and use the same Dialog layout for later editing. This contained flow reuses current APIs rather than introducing a draft-project subsystem.

  Preserve each step's drafts across navigation and retain editable header/addresses after initial creation. Expose narrow child save/status commands for the unified footer and suppress duplicate embedded submit buttons when hosted, with no nested forms. Stage attachment choices locally until explicit Save; retain failed files and upload only pending files. Refresh the owning Project version after successful attachment mutations before later header writes, without replacing unsaved drafts. Disable conflicting Save/navigation during the active mutation. Close after successful saves does not roll back those saves. Retaining a received ID protects optional-step retries; an ambiguous initial-create response is not claimed to be automatically replay-safe.
- Customer-name links in Project List, project property panel and single-project header open the same read-only Popover with basic customer information. Show no estimation dataset, conditions, price adjustments or action buttons. Customer popover clicks must not accidentally select/open a row.
- Project property's Positions tab becomes compact stacked cards showing name, number, modified date, type and thumbnail, with existing navigation semantics.
- Project inner page's property-panel Element editing uses Popover, retaining per-Element expectedVersion and error feedback.

### 4. New Position form and save behavior

Coverage: A22–A31; Q02/Q03.

Rebuild New Position in a two-column PrimeNG Dialog using the directly supplied field groups and [Figma node 10605:88686](https://www.figma.com/design/B9QxH03gmC4CkBTK4iicRO/Planicam--UI-DS-?node-id=10605-88686). Group A: Name, quantity, phase, Brief Description, Model Description. Group B: type, profile system, subsystem, rule package. Group C: fields in width, fields in height, dimensions containing total width, total height, partial width by width-field count, partial height by height-field count. Figma context/screenshot access is currently unverified because the initial connector request failed at transport; retry/inspect before making visual implementation claims.

- Basic information first, including quantity. Position type has an explicit value and no 'System Default'.
- Place a separate selection section after basic information: Position Type -> Profile System -> Sub System and Rule Package. Reset stale dependent selections when a parent changes. Filter from actual compatibility data; visible controls with no options remain disabled. Existing systems stay subject to backend validation. Empty controls are honest missing-data behavior, not completed catalog compatibility; selectable Sub System/Rule Package identity persistence remains subject to the authoritative catalog/input contract.
- Remove the optional 'Rectangular design' checkbox. Required width/height and applicable group fields are always shown/validated for new positions.
- For every Auto-capable input, render a ToggleSwitch beside the input. Auto on disables editing and shows the computed value in that same input; canonical Auto remains null. Recompute through the existing temporary engine as overall dimensions, counts or other manual values change. Manual mode remains editable. Never hide the input to represent Auto.
- Use the original groups and requested two-column layout, avoiding a single long vertical form. Preserve accessible labels/errors and keyboard/focus behavior.
- Extend POST /positions with requested quantity (default one, initially positive within the existing quantity limit) and optional initialDesign:{schemaVersion,input}. The new mandatory-rectangle UI always supplies initialDesign; existing metadata-only callers may omit it. One transaction persists validated envelope metadata, requested physical Elements and the client-produced versioned initial design; backend performs no engineering calculation. Initialized creation becomes IN_PROGRESS; metadata-only creation remains CREATED. This updates the old exact-one/no-design baseline only for the explicitly initialized path after approval. Existing editor initialization reuses Elements and retains its current conflict when already initialized; it is not an idempotent replay API. Preserve the no-automatic-write-replay policy and do not claim transaction atomicity prevents duplicate creation after an ambiguous lost response. Exact initial design contract stays aligned with the current temporary-engine boundary.

### 5. Printout registry and dynamic definition contract

Coverage: P01–P08/P16/P18–P25.

The three concrete planned option definitions are Estimation, Material Analysis and Labor Hours, based on the newly supplied local screenshots and official Orgadata pages. They are planned definitions, not claims of registered generators. Match screenshots by their titles/content: estimation.png -> Estimation; Material analyse.png -> Material Analysis; labor hours.png -> Labor Hours. The last two paths were crossed in the user's reference list. Keep source-supported option fields/defaults/enums distinct from future calculation implementations. Estimation Data navigation buttons and disabled Recalculate behavior are not a license to add backend calculations or executable UI metadata.

Add endpoint (nullable relative API address), icon (frontend semantic registry key), and requiredOptions JSONB to PrintoutType, with migration, PrismaJson annotation and canonical decorated definition-envelope contract. Definitions remain application code owned beside their report generator. Proposed requiredOptions is a read-only persisted projection of the same code-owned definition, never a second editable authority; the registry/seeding path synchronizes it deterministically.

Expose the specified definition fields: code, definitionVersion, supportedFormats, optionsSchema, optionsUi and initialValues, alongside display/category/status/scope and endpoint/icon metadata. Remove canGenerate from backend, frontend models and runtime guards. Only PLANNED and AVAILABLE rows are returned; NEXT and DEPRECATED are excluded. A null endpoint disables selection/generation and gets a compact status tag. AVAILABLE alone never creates an endpoint or generator.

Use JSON Schema draft 2020-12 on both sides. Recommend direct Ajv 8 runtime dependency in each repository, using its 2020-12 validator rather than its default older-draft validator ([official reference](https://ajv.js.org/json-schema.html#draft-2020-12-breaking)). Backend dependency installation requires explicit approval under AGENTS.md. Add format support only when required by an approved real definition. Do not build a partial handwritten JSON Schema validator, import a toolchain's transitive dependency as an application API, introduce Zod, or duplicate option constraints in DTO decorators.

Validate definition/schema/UI consistency before exposure: supported formats, version/code identity, allowed semantic controls, JSON Pointer targets and control/schema compatibility, ordered fields/sections, safe initial-value shape, recognized icon/endpoint policy and schema validity. Required fields may initially be incomplete; their absence must produce normal form errors rather than fabricated defaults.

### 6. Reusable options renderer and wizard

Coverage: P09–P15; W01–W17.

The reusable printout renderer belongs to the owning Hub printout feature; controls are shared-ui primitives. It consumes semantic metadata only, with no Angular selectors, CSS, HTML or executable expressions from the backend.

Map the full requested allowlist: text -> InputText; textarea -> Textarea; number -> InputNumber; select -> Select; multiSelect -> MultiSelect; selectButton -> SelectButton; checkbox -> Checkbox; switch -> ToggleSwitch; date -> DatePicker. Read labels/help from title/description, field order/presentation from optionsUi, and resolve paths using JSON Pointer. Unsupported/inconsistent definitions are blocked with an understandable error.

- Step 1 Printouts: searchable category Accordions, individual checkboxes, whole-category select with indeterminate state, select/clear all, selected report summary/removal and icon/format metadata. Select all/category toggles apply to eligible matching search results; disabled endpoints are never selected. Category indeterminate state reflects eligible matching children. Global Clear all clears the full selection, including reports outside the current search; searching alone never clears selections.
- Step 2 Elements: search, Type/System Select filters, Show selected ToggleSwitch, checkbox/header selection, complete scoped Element list with thumbnail/name/number/type/dimensions/system, counts and selected thumbnail summary. Select all matches covers the filtered context, including matches not yet fetched; it is not a current-page checkbox. Preserve actual Element IDs and current exclusion/archive rules; never silently substitute Position IDs for the requested elementIds payload. Explicit ELEMENTS and FABRICATION_BATCH entry contexts retain their original physical subset and cannot expand to sibling Elements just because they share a Position.
- Step 3 Options: per-report navigation with completion states and progress, independently selected supported formats using multi-select SelectButton, schema-driven sections, reset current report, field-path errors, next incomplete report and view-elements navigation. Initialize once from initialValues; switching reports/steps preserves edits and each report's formats. Reset options resets only the current report's option values from initialValues; selected output formats remain intact.
- A report is ready only when its options validate and at least one unique supported format is selected. Review requires every selected report ready and valid element selection. Required means present: false and 0 can be valid. Nonempty text uses minLength where specified. Do not populate schema default values automatically.
- Step 4 Review: printout table with category/formats/options summary/status and edit controls; selected Elements in an Accordion (not row expansion); generation summary, per-format/total file counts, edit-selection links and sticky footer. Each report-format pair is one output file.
- Results: implement workflow/result contracts and UI states for progress/success/partial failure, per-file reason/Download/Retry, retry-failed-only, Download ready files ZIP, back to settings, another set and Done. Already successful files remain available and are not regenerated by Retry failed. Under the user's explicit workflow-only scope, verify these states with isolated fixtures; no production report generation or downloadable fabricated files are added. All unimplemented production generators remain disabled with null endpoints.

### 7. Submission, validation, generation and storage

Coverage: P16–P19; Q03/Q04.

Submit values only: elementIds and printouts[{code,definitionVersion,formats,options}]. class-validator validates the request envelope. The backend resolves its own registered definition and endpoint handler, rejects unknown/non-generatable codes, validates options with that schema, validates unique supported formats, and checks tenant/access/eligible inputs. Do not trust schema/UI metadata, tenant IDs, storage paths, remote URLs or generator code supplied by the client.

Return field errors scoped by printout and JSON Pointer. Return a recognizable stale-definition-version error; frontend reloads the definition and makes any invalidated user choices visible rather than silently submitting an old contract. Neither errors nor reloading may destroy unrelated report edits.

Define request/run identity, report-format output identity, per-file status/error and authorized download reference as workflow contracts. Failed-only retry references failed outputs from that run, not a blind replay of successful outputs. Back to settings preserves drafts, Generate another set starts a fresh selection, and Done returns to the originating context. Actual registered generators and production generation/download/ZIP routes are outside this clarified assignment. Their future implementation must create immutable GeneratedPrintout/StorageFileAsset outputs, enforce tenant access and financial prerequisites, and preserve partial successes. Do not add placeholder production handlers that pretend to generate or expose fabricated files.

### 8. Verification and independent acceptance

Coverage: Q01–Q07 and every A/P/W criterion above.

After plan approval, use the repository's scoped crew authorization for focused endpoint/UI checks and isolated data. Backend: schema validation/generation/build and no-fix lint; contracts, registry consistency, tenant rejection, stale versions, missing/false/zero values, extra/unsupported values, duplicate formats, eligible atomic batch assignment and atomic Position quantity/initialization. Frontend: affected lint/build/boundary checks plus focused browser flows at supported desktop sizes, real overlay anchoring/focus/keyboard, no horizontal modal overflow, complete list access beyond old page limits, row-select/link-open separation, cascades/Auto values, every wizard transition/edit/validation, and genuine retry/download outcomes when generators exist.

Reviewer independently inspects original criteria, docs, actual diff and allowed runtime evidence. Engineer corrects findings; reviewer rechecks; Atlas accepts integration. Every acceptance ID must have a result. Unexecuted or blocked checks stay labeled unverified.

Complete owning docs/READMEs and applicable uncommitted changesets under the approved Git exception. Save one verified outcome report for this top-level assignment only, explicitly recording that all rework is uncommitted by direct user instruction. Report remaining blockers honestly; no merge, push, PR, release, branch deletion or user-acceptance claim.

## Clarifications and approval record

1. Resolved by direct user reply: Position Groups A/B/C and Figma node 10605:88686 supplied. Inspect high-fidelity Figma context/screenshot before implementation; initial connector transport failed.
2. Resolved by direct user reply: three Logikal screenshots and official docs supplied, and printout scope explicitly workflow/contracts with unimplemented generators disabled and endpoint null. Verify result states using isolated fixtures, not production generator success claims.
3. Approved with the linked plan: printout JSONB projection/code authority, Ajv 8 direct dependencies, no-visible-pagination with complete bounded loading, visible disabled empty Sub System/Rule Package selectors until real catalog data exists, and atomic quantity/design Position creation. These are approved implementation decisions, not yet implemented facts.
4. Git resolved by direct user choice: implement on current branches, preserve all existing staging and leave the rework uncommitted. This overrides the crew's normal milestone/changeset commit steps for this assignment. Do not commit the existing Hub foundation.

The invoked [Redhat Crew skill](D:/Planicam/planicam-workspace/.agents/skills/redhat-crew/SKILL.md) initial-plan approval requirement is satisfied by the direct user confirmation. Apply the explicit current-branch/no-commit exception above; do not ask again for already approved scope.
